defaults.permitted_development: A rear extension can be permitted development in Scotland outside conservation areas where it stays within the Scottish rear-extension height, depth, footprint and boundary limits.

rules.height_rules: Single-storey rear extensions should have eaves at or below 3m and overall height at or below 4m, with parts within 1m of a boundary no higher than 2.5m. More-than-one-storey rear extensions should not be higher than the existing house.
rules.depth_rules: Single-storey rear projection is up to 3m on a terraced house or 4m on other houses. More-than-one-storey rear extensions should stay rear-only and within a footprint no larger than the original dwellinghouse.
rules.boundary_rules: Single-storey work within 1m of a boundary should stay at or below 2.5m. More-than-one-storey rear extensions should be at least 10m from the curtilage boundary.
rules.roof_rules: The roof should stay subordinate to the house and avoid creating a visually dominant rear block. A simple roof form is usually easier to defend than a bulky high ridge close to the boundary.
rules.materials_rules: Use materials and detailing that sit appropriately with the existing house.
